newsitem.title: USA: Pena seeks option to proposed 2002 US SPR sale.
newsitem.headline: Pena seeks option to proposed 2002 US SPR sale.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Federico Pena said Thursday he will look for alternatives to the sale of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in 2002 called for in the White House proposed budget.
Speaking at a Senate Appropriations subcommittee hearing, Pena described the proposed sale as a "marker" and said he will look for other options.
"Some of these place markers are there for a reason and I believe we've got to look for other ways to make a cut," Pena said.
The Clinton budget called for selling $1.1 billion worth of oil from the SPR in 2002 to help balance the budget.
Pena said the administration did not propose any SPR sales for the next fiscal year.
